title: Measures to Improve Safety on the Roads and Increase Penalties following Recent Spate of Fatal Accidents
what_it_is: Measures to Improve Safety on the Roads and Increase Penalties following Recent Spate of Fatal Accidents

sections.label: Road traffic fatal accidents questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Home Affairs about causes of fatal accidents, mitigation plans, penalties, enforcement and driver education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in view of the recent spate of major road traffic fatal accidents (a) what are the typical causes of such accidents; (b) what mitigation plans will the Ministry implement; and (c) whether there is a need to raise the relevant penalties under the Road Traffic Act 1961.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) over the past five years, how many fatal accidents have occurred due to reckless driving and speeding; (b) whether there is a need to review the existing penalties under the Road Traffic Act 1961; (c) whether the Ministry and LTA will consider stricter enforcement measures or legislative changes to ensure greater accountability and discourage dangerous driving; and (d) whether there are plans to intensify campaigns or programmes in educating drivers on speeding and reckless driving and increase road safety awareness.

sections.label: Road safety improvement measures questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Home Affairs about improving road safety, enforcement, easier public reporting and smart cameras at junctions and zebra crossings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the significant increase of traffic accidents resulting in fatalities in 2023 and the recent road accident in Tampines that claimed lives, what measures can be taken to improve road safety for users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in view of the recent fatal traffic accidents (a) how will enforcement of road safety for both motorists and pedestrians be further enhanced; (b) whether the reporting of drivers' infringement of traffic rules by the public can be made easier; and (c) whether smart enforcement cameras can be installed at all major traffic junctions and zebra crossings.

sections.label: Accident statistics over five years
sections.summary: Injury or fatal accidents fell about 10% from 7,822 in 2019 to 7,075 in 2023, while fatal accidents rose about 12% from 117 to 131.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In the last five years, the number of accidents resulting in injuries or fatalities has fallen by about 10%, from 7,822 in 2019, to 7,075 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: By this measure, our roads have become safer.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: However, if we look at the number of accidents resulting in fatalities, this has increased by about 12%, from 117 in 2019, to 131 in 2023.

sections.label: Dangerous driving causing death penalty
sections.summary: Under the RTA, a first-time offender for dangerous driving causing death is liable for imprisonment of two to eight years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Under the RTA, for an offence of dangerous driving causing death, a first-time offender is liable for imprisonment of two to eight years.

sections.label: Traffic Police intensified ad hoc enforcements
sections.summary: In the last six weeks the Traffic Police intensified ad hoc enforcements, detecting close to 1,400 violations and arresting 29 motorists.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Traffic Police (TP) has in the last six weeks, also intensified ad hoc enforcements, which has detected close to 1,400 violations and arrested 29 motorists for traffic-related and other offences.

sections.label: Traffic Police road safety videos
sections.summary: The Traffic Police is intensifying education and engagement efforts and will publish a series of road safety videos in the second half of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Traffic Police (TP) has also been intensifying its education and engagement efforts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: TP will be publishing a series of road safety videos in the second half of 2024.

sections.label: Refresher course for drivers
sections.summary: The refresher course caters to drivers who have not driven for several years, and mandating it for all motorists is not considered useful.

sentences.text: It caters to drivers who have not driven for several years.
We do not think it is useful to mandate the refresher course for all motorists.

sections.label: Causes of most accidents
sections.summary: Most accidents happen because of poor road behaviour rather than inexperience.

sentences.text: Most accidents happen because of poor road behaviour, rather than inexperience.

sections.label: 2023 speeding accident figure
sections.summary: The 2023 figure for speeding related accidents is the lowest between 2017 and 2023.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The 2023 figure for speeding related accidents is lowest between 2017 and 2023.

sections.label: Speeding accidents and red-light cameras
sections.summary: Speeding related accidents fell from 757 in 2020 to 624 in 2023, and red-light cameras detecting speeding started on 1 April to add deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, the number of speeding related accidents in 2020 was 757.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: However, in 2023, it went down to 624.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Essentially, we are seeing a reduction in the number of speeding related accidents.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, we continue to do this and with the new device that we have started on 1 April – the red-light cameras that can detect the speeding element – we hope that will provide additional deterrence so that people will be mindful before they speed.

sections.label: Traffic violation reports received
sections.summary: Around 30,000 traffic violation reports are received every year on average, showing many members of the public can access the e-services.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: This is in addition to the platforms that we have, which I had shared earlier, in reply to Ms Tin Pei Ling's queries.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, on average, we receive around 30,000 traffic violation reports such as these every year, which shows many members of the public are already able to access the e-services.

sections.label: Numbers of TP officers
sections.summary: The numbers of TP officers have been going up since 2022.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For the numbers of TP officers, in fact, the numbers have been going up since 2022.

sections.label: Careless driving jail terms
sections.summary: Careless driving causing death carries up to three years' jail for a first offence, and grievous bodily harm up to two years, both doubled for repeat offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Currently, I think for careless driving, if it causes death, it is up to three years in jail for the first offence and double for repeat offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For grievous bodily harm, it is up to two years in jail or double for repeat offences.

sections.label: Refining sentencing guidelines application
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Government would consider applying sentencing guidelines, such as the two to eight years, more stringently within legislated punishment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can I ask whether in light of the recent serious accidents, would the Government look into the possibility of refining the application of the sentencing guidelines, for example, the two to eight years, but perhaps applying more stringently as compared to the past, but still keeping within the punishment legislated?

sections.label: Sentencing based on culpability
sections.summary: The Government will look at the facts of each case and exercise what the law provides commensurate with the culpability of the person who caused the accident.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: With regard to the first supplementary question, we look at the facts of the case.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: I assure the Member that we will exercise what we are provided for under the law to commensurate with the culpability of the person who caused the accident.

sections.label: Broad-based road safety culture
sections.summary: The Member asks whether TP could look into how society can help one another make roads safer, as it is about a broad-based safety culture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Whereas in some other countries that I have been to, you will see other motorists, the moment you exceed the speed limit, other motorists honk at you to slow down.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I wonder whether TP could look into this aspect and see how society, as a whole, we can help one another to make the road safer because, after all, it is not about cameras and about TP being everywhere, but it is really about a broad-based safety culture that we all want to have.

sections.label: Emotional stress causing road behaviour
sections.summary: Road rage, inability to give way, anxiety and impatience stem from emotional and mental stresses that people may not be able to regulate themselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Because a lot of these examples of road rage, inability to give way, anxiety and impatience on the roads are actually stemming from a lot of emotional and mental stresses that people may not be able to regulate themselves.
